title: Legislative districts of Surigao del Sur
wikitext:
{{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Surigao del Sur''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Surigao del Sur]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Surigao}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Surigao del Sur were represented under the former province of [[Surigao (province)|Surigao]] (1907–1961). The enactment of Republic Act No. 2786 on June 19, 1960 split the old Surigao province into [[Surigao del Norte]] and [[Surigao del Sur]], and provided the new provinces separate representations in Congress.{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 2786 - An Act to Create the Provinces of Surigao del Norte and Surigao del Sur|date=June 19, 1960|access-date=August 9, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno2786.html}} The new province of Surigao del Sur first elected its [[#Lone District (defunct)|own representative]] in the [[1961 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1961 elections]]. Surigao del Sur was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XI]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. The province was reapportioned into [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|two congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 21, 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == 1st District == *'''[[Cities of the Philippines|City]]''': [[Tandag]] (became city 2007) *'''[[Municipalities of the Philippines|Municipalities]]''': [[Bayabas, Surigao del Sur|Bayabas]], [[Cagwait, Surigao del Sur|Cagwait]], [[Cantilan, Surigao del Sur|Cantilan]], [[Carmen, Surigao del Sur|Carmen]], [[Carrascal, Surigao del Sur|Carrascal]], [[Cortes, Surigao del Sur|Cortes]], [[Lanuza, Surigao del Sur|Lanuza]], [[Lianga, Surigao del Sur|Lianga]], [[Madrid, Surigao del Sur|Madrid]], [[Marihatag, Surigao del Sur|Marihatag]], [[San Agustin, Surigao del Sur|San Agustin]], [[San Miguel, Surigao del Sur|San Miguel]], [[Tago, Surigao del Sur|Tago]] *'''Population (2020)''': 369,785{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|access-date=November 21, 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
